device.name: Building Energy Storage Simulation (battery, solar and price-varying grid)

facts.text: The action space is Box(low=-1, high=1, shape=(1,)): one float per step, the fraction of the battery's maximum charge per time step
A step multiplies the action by max_battery_charge_per_timestep and passes the result to the battery
The battery trims the charge or discharge amount to +-max_battery_charge_per_timestep and clamps the state of charge to 0..capacity
Electricity consumption is the battery energy plus the load minus the solar generation, and a negative value is trimmed to 0 so surplus solar energy is not fed into the grid
The reward is -1 * electricity_consumption * electricity_price
The observation concatenates the battery state of charge with the load, solar and price forecasts, 3*n+1 numbers in that order
The observation space is Box(-inf, inf, shape=(num_forecasting_steps*3+1,))
step returns terminated when step_count reaches max_timesteps and truncated is always False
Environment.reset() calls BuildingSimulation.reset()
BuildingSimulation.reset() resets the battery state of charge and sets step_count to 0
With randomize_start_time_step the reset draws start_index from numpy's global uniform generator; the seed argument of reset is not used
The Environment constructor defaults max_timesteps to 2000 and num_forecasting_steps to 4
The constructor asserts that max_timesteps plus num_forecasting_steps is not greater than the profile length
The default profiles are loaded from the package's data/preprocessed CSVs: electricity_load_profile.csv, solar_generation_profile.csv and electricity_price_profile.csv
BuildingSimulation converts a scalar electricity_price into a constant profile of the same length as the solar generation profile
Environment.step takes the first element of an iterable action and passes it to the simulation without checking it against the action space; the OpenMHS runtime enforces the Box bound instead
The documented usage constructs Environment(building_simulation=simulation) and then calls env.reset() and env.step(1)
The README documents the action interval [-1;1]: 1 is maximum charging defined by max_battery_charge_per_timestep, -1 maximum discharging and 0 neither
The README documents the observation table: the state of charge in kWh, then n load, n solar and n price forecasts
The README states that the episode ends when max_timesteps is reached

determinism.notes: the dynamics are deterministic; upstream reset(seed) ignores the seed and, with randomize_start_time_step, draws the start index from numpy's global generator, while this package's fake seeds a private random.Random when a seed is supplied, so a seed does not give the same trajectory on the two; no snapshot or restore exists, so repeatability is claimed only for a fresh world

gaps: analytic energy accounting, not a physical model: one row of the supplied profiles per step, an ideal battery with only a state of charge, and no electrical, thermal, aging, efficiency, inverter or control dynamics, no forces or contacts and no actuator, sensor or noise model

timestep_ms is 0 because the Environment class declares no duration for one time step; a step consumes one row of the load, solar and price profiles, and ticks advance that row index (fidelity F0 is not a claim about elapsed time)
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and only commands advance the world

the fake backend synthesizes placeholder profile rows and re-implements Environment, BuildingSimulation and Battery in pure Python; it was not compared with the upstream environment (gymnasium is not importable where the gate runs), so observations, rewards and prices are not the bundled CSV data and the fake returns Python float lists where upstream returns a numpy array
the fake's optional forecast randomisation changes only the returned copy, while upstream adds the noise in place to a numpy slice of the stored profile
no rendering (upstream render is a no-op), no snapshot or restore (the environment has no get_state/set_state pair), and reset options are accepted and ignored as the upstream reset ignores them
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
